```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Distribution and billing come built in. A has a named, sourced, low-cost channel: Shopify App Store ads start at $5/day, and one developer reported install costs about a third of other networks. B's sourced channels are worse for a solo operator. Google CPC averages $5.42. Product Hunt results swing from 68 signups out of 170 visitors to 50 signups out of 20,000.",
    "A has a clearer gap left by the free incumbent. Shopify Magic is sourced as not handling alt text, images, titles, or bulk editing. AltText.ai's 141 reviews at 4.5 stars show merchants already pay for the alt-text and image half of the product. B's brief says free tiers are standard (50% of 62 tools) and that incumbents already ship AI triage and MCP integrations, which leaves no obvious unclaimed wedge.",
    "A carries a lighter trust and compliance load for a first sale. B is an embedded, customer-facing widget that processes end-user data. It needs a DPA, a privacy policy, and records of processing, and buyers may expect SOC2-level assurance from a single unknown vendor. A sells to small merchants inside Shopify's ecosystem, at $12-$19/mo entry pricing, which is easier to try on impulse.",
    "A's demand evidence comes from buyers. It cites three independent merchant threads describing description writing as time-consuming or procrastinated. B's demand evidence is thinner and partly undercuts willingness to pay, as explained in the weakest-evidence field.",
    "Both markets are saturated, but A's competitors with few or no reviews (Descrii 0, Gelo.ai 3, Describly 1 negative) point to low-quality rivals that a reliable alt-text and bulk-focused entrant could beat. B faces 73 tracked tools with commoditized ~$29/mo entry pricing."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence is the weakest item. The pain quote comes from an Indie Hackers post by a builder promoting their own feedback widget, so it is a competitor's marketing, not a buyer's need. The only other quote is a prospective buyer calling $50-80/month for a feedback widget 'ridiculous', which signals price resistance rather than willingness to pay. The supporting claim of '20+ near-identical' products found in organic search has no specific source.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs describe crowded, commoditized categories, and neither shows evidence that a new entrant reached paying customers quickly. A's case leans on several soft points. The ADA settlement figures come from vendor blogs with an interest in selling compliance. The App Store ad efficiency claim is a single developer's anecdote. The Reddit demand quotes concern description writing, which free Shopify Magic partly covers. A wins mainly on distribution, compliance burden, and the alt-text and bulk gap, not on strong proof of demand."
}
```
